## Description

Before starting directly to build the project always try to build a basic schema in your head about how your project will look and what it will comprise or you can also use some drawing tools that are available on the internet.

For this project, let's start with the basic layout of our landing page. At first, the whole webpage or let's say the landing page is divided into 3 parts: **Header**, **Main**, **and Footer**. You need to divide the HTML body into these three parts. The `header` tag contains the navbar of the landing page, the `main` tag contains the main content of the landing page, and the `footer` tag contains the footer of the landing page.

Now, let's set the `height` of our body and then the height of the sections i.e. header, main, and footer of our landing page. You have to set the maximum height of the body to `100%` of the viewable screen's height. Make sure to use the `vh` unit while setting the height of the body.

Select the `header`, `main`, and `footer` and set their minimum height to `10%`, `60%` and `30%` of the viewable screen's height. Here also, you need to use the `vh` unit to set their sizes.



Because the viewport height of the devices may not be the same so we cannot use the absolute units therefore prefer to use the `vh` unit in this project.

## Objectives

In this stage, you should have created the following in your first landing webpage:

- Divide the webpage into three parts i.e. **Header**, **Main**, **and Footer** and the order of the division should be the same as mentioned here.
- The maximum height of the body tag and the minimum height of the header, main and footer tag should be set as per the above-mentioned rules.

## Example

![An outline of the layout of the elements of the future First Landing site](https://ucarecdn.com/74687e06-c86e-4232-996c-a0dd9e0608ec/)
title: Layout

## Description

Our first landing page now has a basic layout. In this stage, you are going to add a Navbar to your webpage.

As you already know, the navbar is present inside the `header` tag. Let's start adding the `nav` tag inside the `header` tag. The navbar contains four anchor elements i.e. four hyperlinks and all four have different `id` attributes as given below:

- `link_logo`
- `link_home`
- `link_product`
- `link_contact`

The first link having the id as `link_logo` goes to the *home* section which has an id as `home` and you are going to create this section in the next stage. For now, link the first anchor tag to the `home`. This anchor tag also contains an image that will be the logo of your webpage. The image should have a fixed width of `64` and height of `64` . Don't forget to add the `title` and `alt` attributes to improve the accessibility of your webpage.

The second anchor tag having the id as `link_home` also goes to the *home* section. The third and fourth anchor tag having the id as `link_product` and `link_contact` goes to the *product* and *contact* section which will be created in the next stages. The texts for all these three anchor tags (second, third and fourth) must be Home, Product, and Contact respectively.

Let's set the maximum width of the `nav` tag to `100%` and as you know to align the content of the nav in a horizontal direction you have to set the display of the nav tag to `flex` with the items wrapped.

For the navbar, you can add the paddings and margins to create the space you like. You can also change the color of the links and remove the text decoration if you want to as given in the example below.

## Objectives

In this stage, you should have created the following in your first landing webpage:

- The `nav` tag is present inside the `header` tag.
- There should be four anchor tags with the above-mentioned IDs inside the nav tag.
- There is an image inside the first anchor tag and the above-mentioned conditions should be fulfilled.
- The first and second anchor tag should go to the *home*.
- The third and fourth anchor tag should go to *product* and *contact*.
- The texts of these anchor tags must be the same as mentioned above.
- The nav tag should have a maximum width of `100%` and all the CSS properties that are mentioned above related to the `nav` tag should be present.

## Example

![Detailed design navigation bar and draft layout template for the First Landing site](https://ucarecdn.com/020f53f2-8d74-4a16-a558-11f044870229/)
title: Navbar

## Description

Let's start to create the Product banner for your landing page!

First, start by creating a `div` inside the `main` tag. This `div` will contain your banner; it should have an id of `home`. Inside this div, there should be a first-level `heading`, `paragraph`, and an `anchor` tag. This anchor tag goes to or is hyperlinked to the *product* section of the page. You can add any text of your choice in the heading, paragraph, and anchor tag. You can style the paragraph as you like but the example paragraph has adjusted font-size and font-weight.

To stop overflowing the content of the div having an id of `home`, set the correct CSS property such that the overflow of the content is **hidden** and make sure that the text inside the div having an id of `home` is centered.

The anchor tag should look like a **button,** so to make it look like a basic button you need to add a border with solid lines with `1px` thickness and remove the text-decoration. The example button has border-radius, font-size, padding, color and background-color adjusted.

## Objectives

In this stage, you should have created the following in your first landing webpage:

- A new div having an id of `home` inside the `main` tag.
- Inside the div with an id of `home`, there is a first-level `heading`, `paragraph`, and an `anchor` tag present which is hyperlinked to the `product`.
- The content of the div having an id of `home`, if overflown, should be **hidden** and the texts should be **center-aligned**.
- The anchor tag should look like a button and the CSS properties to apply the same are mentioned above.

## Example

![Product banner for the First Landing site](https://ucarecdn.com/43349425-05e8-4d89-847f-294e3bffcc3a/)
title: Product banner

having an id of `product` just after the div having an id of `home`. This div contains two more divs having an id of `col-1` and `col-2`. You can think of the outer div as a container acting as a row and the other two divs that are direct children as columns. Each of the divs having id of `col-1` and `col-2` contains a **div** and an **image** for the content. The divs present inside the div having an id of `col-1` and `col-2` has a second-level heading and a paragraph too. If these statements don't look promising you can refer to the below representation to get an actual flow of the layout. Here is an example of the above-explained structure: ```html
``` You can increase the number of `div` rows, but the tests will only check for the first one. Now, you are done with creating a basic layout for the Product gallery. Let's apply some CSS to style whatever you've created using HTML. The display of the div having an id of `product` should be `flex` and the items shouldn't wrap. ## Description Until now, the header and the main section of your landing page must be completed. It's time to create a footer for your landing page. Start by adding a new `div` having an id of `contact` to the `footer` tag . Now, add one more `div` with an id of `contact-col1` inside the `div` having an id of `contact` and this acts as a column which is present inside the outer div which acts as a row. This column `div`(div having an id of `contact-col1`) will contain the same navigation links and the logo **image** from the navbar. Check out this example structure to better understand: ```html
``` So, the first link inside the div having an id of `contact-col1`, which goes to the home link, will contain the logo *image* with an id of `footer_link_logo`, width and height of `64`, same as mentioned in the header section, and the other anchor tags will be grouped inside another container `div` and the ids of these anchor tags are mentioned below. After this container `div` there is a `p` tag with a text of your choice, it could be the current year. The ids of the anchor tags - `footer_link_home` - `footer_link_product` - `footer_link_contact` These three anchor tags inside a div container must be hyperlinked to the *home*, *product*, and *contact* in the given order as it was done while creating the header section. The content of these anchor tags must be **Home**, **Product**, and **Contact** in the given order. Now, let's apply the styles to your footer section. The footer tag has a **maximum width** of `100%`. The div having an id of `contact` should have the display value of `flex` and the items must be wrapped. The div having an id of `contact-col1` should have a maximum width of `100%`. The example has extra paddings and margins, you can choose to add them. ## Objectives In this stage your website should have: - A new `div` with the id of `contact` in the `footer `tag; - A `div` container inside the `contact` `div` that has the same navigation links and logo image from the `navbar`; - The first link with the logo image inside with the conditions mentioned above; - Wrap other links inside the `div`; - The `paragraph` tag a text; - All tags should follow their styles described above. ## Example ![Footer for the First Landing project](https://ucarecdn.com/01bab842-a2b5-4cf8-a492-c043e07e76d8/)
title: Footer

## Description

In this stage, you are going to add a contact form to your footer.

Start by adding a new `div` with the id of `contact-col2` i.e. adding another column after the div having an id of `contact-col1`. This div or this column will have a `form` tag. It will collect the visitor's info.

The first child element inside the **form** tag is the heading of **level 5**. After this heading, there are two divs present.

The **first div** contains a `label` and an input tag with an id of `email`. Visitors will input their emails, so the label should say **Email** and the input type should also be `email`.

The **second div** contains a `label`. Inside, there will be a **checkbox** input and a **text**. Also, donÔÇÖt forget the *for* attributes for labels.

Both of the inputs should be required to fill in and they should be inside their respective labels.

The last item inside a `form` is a submit button with any text. Now, let's add some styles to our footer page.

The div having an id of `contact-col2 `should have a maximum width of 100%.

When submitted, if everything goes well, the page should be refreshed. If users fail to enter any values, the browser should notify them that the input is required.

## Objectives

In this stage your website should have:

- A new `div` inside the contact `div` with a `form` inside;
- A level five `heading` tag inside the `form`;
- A `div` container wrapping a label and an input for email;
- A `div` container wrapping a label and a checkbox;
- A submit button for the `form`;
- The page should refresh after submitting the form;
- All inputs are required before submitting;
- All tags must have the styles described above.
